This should be the highest priority fix possibly besides core stability, and should push down features. Security in a network-focused application must be among the highest priorities, and in order for security to be correct, a client should never trust a message received from any source besides an authenticated central server.

Thank you for your feedback!

Last year, we made some improvements to make portals more secure. Most notably, users can now create locked instances, and we've added an optional prompt before being taken through a portal.

Please let us know if you have any feedback regarding our new portals. Some of your requests haven't been addressed (yet!), and separate Canny requests would make it easier for us to track which of your request have and haven't been fulfilled yet.

details:
I think everyone in VRChat has already seen how some users can create dozens of portals with an infinite timer on behalf of other users, move them or put them directly in front of other users. This has been happening for many years. Portals are probably the only mechanics that have existed since "ancient" times and have not undergone any changes from the security system. At the moment, portals are the most insecure application mechanics. Today, portals are one of the main tools for mod clients to attack other users. As I understand it, when you switched to IL2CPP, you thought that mod clients would be almost impossible and difficult to implement, so you just ignored all the security problems, hoping that everything would resolve itself. But this is not the case, less than six months have passed, as every second schoolboy visitor has a mod client, using which is used to disturb and annoy users. I believe that the system of moving between instances of worlds should be completely redesigned.

What do I offer on security issues:

1. Portals should become a separate mechanic in the app, not just a component on the prefab. At the moment, creating portals is not much different from instantiating any prefab. This is not correct. Portals should be created by a separate application mechanic under full control and all checks.

2. Portals should not be triggered just by touching. There must be unobtrusive confirmation. At least for non-friends portals for sure. I believe that the correct approach would be to make the portal appear small initially at the user's eye level, then the user approaches and interacts with the portal with their hands, as a result of which the portal expands and shows an interface with additional information, where the user can click "enter the portal". (Who came up with the idea to place information above the portal? Is it convenient for you to lift your head up every time?)

3. The client must locally track user requests to create portals and delete the previous one, and should not expect the creator to send a request to remove copies of a portal, should not expect correct timer value, ...

4. You need to check the data that users submit. Manipulations with special characters (in particular with NUL 0x00) cause you to break the interface lines and create portals as if they were created by other users. This is a serious problem, since the user who is abusing the isuue using mod client can stay on the sidelines and substitute other non-guilty users.

5. Why can an instance ID consist of letters at all? If you decide that the instance ID is a random integer, is it really that hard to make sure that the user sends a number instead of an arbitrary string? Why is it necessary to send a string at all? Because of parameters like privte/hidden/nonce/..? So why not make them separate properties? In my opinion, encoding and decoding parameters in one line is a bad idea.

6. The principle, "if I was once in intanse, I can always get there again and get anyone with me" is very unsafe and not obvious to new users. For those who do not know: if you are in any non-public instance, then you know its ID, and knowing the instance ID, any user can log in without confirmation. This also applies to friends-only instances, which can be accessed by completely unknown users if you pass them an ID. Moreover, you can do this without the mod clients - just take the ID of the current instance from the API or logs, and create a link to the instance manually. I believe that this is not correct and there should be a more complex security system of "passes", so that even if you know the ID, you can only join by confirming the owner.

7. owned-public instances, such that they are completely public, but they have a Creator-owner (or maybe more than one) who has moderation rights in this instance. This can be useful for various types of public events and meetups.

8. Legalize the ability to create portals that lead to friends, including non-public instances. Now this is already possible with mod clients. I think this is very convenient. If p.6. if implemented, this function will be completely safe.

9. In the end, portals should not lag. Even legally installed portals cause noticeable fps drawdowns, both due to GPU load and due to massive Api requests to servers and RPC between users.

What I also suggest on other issues:

1. Inside the portals, you display a preview of the world. I understand that the point is to show that there is another world behind the portal and it is as if it is visible through the portal. Well, it's a good idea, but it's better to let users upload cubemap and display it in portals. In this way, the portal can be viewed from different angles and view the environment.

2. allow authors to create stationary portals in worlds with the ability to go to the same instance ID, but in a different world. This will allow you to split large worlds into smaller ones and allow users to move freely between segments without the fear of "getting lost" in different instances when passing through different portals at different times. To protect against instance overflow, it may make sense to count the number of hosts in the sum of the world group and the instance ID data. Perhaps, for this purpose, it makes sense to formalize the concept of a group of worlds. In General, there is something to think about, and I suggest giving the authors more opportunities to link portals not just worlds, but also instances.

3. This does not apply to direct portals, but I believe that authors should be able to block public instances completely for the chosen world. This makes sense, for example, for the worlds of movie theater and complex games, where publicity can cause significant difficulties, where it will be difficult to get peace or focus. Of course, the non-publicity of worlds should not affect their popularity and appearance in the ranking of worlds.

4. Preload the world before leaving the previous instance. Some applications similar to VRChat already know how to do this and it is very convenient. What is the point of sitting, waiting, and watching the progressbar load? You can do this in the background, and when everything is ready, you can notify the user that they are ready to log in to the new instance.

5. The choice of instance on the stationary portal. Why does the user get sent to a random instance when logging in to the portal? Why is there no choice? Why can't I suggest that the user immediately make a non-public intsans?
title: Portals are completely insecure and require a complete review. For several years now, portals have been one of the main ways of abuse (using modified clients).
